claims.claim_text: Red Star interprets comments from a former DSA staffer as affirming that DSA's social-democratic wing and aligned staffers operate as a party of professional reformists, although Michael Harrington likely did not intend to create one.
Red Star criticizes a view that DSA members are too unreliable and transient to plan and direct strategic campaigns, so paid staffers should do that political work.
Red Star describes a staff-led organizational model relegating most DSA members to canvassing, phone banking, text banking, and funding the organization through dues.
Red Star argues that a staff-led DSA relegating most members to campaign grunt work and dues payments does not value members as thinkers, organizers, leaders, or decision makers.
Red Star views the staff-led organizational model relegating DSA members to campaign grunt work and dues payments as a failure.
DSA has not persuaded non-socialist legislators to back reforms like Medicare for All, the Green New Deal, and the PRO Act.
Losing the Bowman and Bush seats shows there is no clear path to a socialist legislative supermajority.
In the post-2016 era, DSA’s strength and success has come primarily from the organizing work of its locals.
DSA has flourished not as a vehicle for national reform campaigns, but as a laboratory where socialists have learned and grown through organizing experience and dialogue with one another.
